title: Rhubarb and custard cake
subtitle: a vanilla custard-scented sponge layered with roasted rhubarb and custard buttercream
excerpt: Rhubarb and custard cake is a vanilla sponge filled with roasted rhubarb and a custard-flavoured buttercream. The rhubarb is roasted with sugar until tender and jammy, then cooled before layering. The sponge itself is flavoured with a little custard powder, giving the crumb a pale yellow colour and a vanilla-forward warmth that mirrors the classic rhubarb and custard sweet.
sourceNotes: Rhubarb and custard as a flavour combination is deeply embedded in British confectionery and pudding culture, most familiar from the classic hard-boiled sweet. Using this combination in a layer cake reflects a broader trend of British bakers drawing on nostalgic sweet flavours from the 2000s onward.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The roasted rhubarb can be made 2 days ahead. Assemble the day of serving; keep refrigerated.

content.text: Rhubarb and custard cake plays on the classic British sweet: a vanilla and custard-flavoured sponge paired with sharp roasted rhubarb. The sponge has custard powder in the batter which gives it a creamy colour and a stronger vanilla warmth. The rhubarb is roasted separately until tender and jammy, then cooled and layered with a custard-flavoured buttercream between the sponges.

Roast the rhubarb: toss the pieces with the 60 g caster sugar and vanilla in a small baking dish. Roast at 200 degrees C (fan 180 degrees C / gas 6) for 15 to 20 minutes until tender but still holding its shape. Drain the excess liquid and leave to cool. Reserve a few pieces for decoration.
Reduce the oven to 180 degrees C (fan 160 degrees C / gas 4). Grease and line two 20 cm sandwich tins.

Beat the softened butter and caster sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time with the vanilla. Sift in the flour, custard powder, and baking powder. Add the milk and fold until just combined.
Divide the batter between the tins. Bake for 25 to 28 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tins for 15 minutes, then turn out and cool completely.

Make the custard buttercream: beat the butter until pale. Mix the custard powder with the milk to a smooth paste. Beat into the butter, then add the sifted icing sugar in two additions and beat until smooth.

Spread a generous layer of custard buttercream on one sponge. Spoon the cooled roasted rhubarb over the buttercream. Place the second sponge on top and press gently. Spread or swirl the remaining buttercream on top. Arrange a few reserved rhubarb pieces to decorate.

attrs.problem: Rhubarb too wet and making the cake soggy
attrs.avoid: Avoid using rhubarb that has released a lot of juice without draining it; the liquid will soak into the sponge.
attrs.fix: Drain the roasted rhubarb well before layering. Allowing it to cool on a rack rather than in the dish lets more liquid drain away.

attrs.avoid: Avoid adding the custard paste while the butter is cold or adding the icing sugar before the custard is fully beaten in.
attrs.fix: Beat the butter until very soft and pale before adding anything. Dissolve the custard powder in the milk fully before adding to prevent lumps.
